transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Leo (Redwood Console PM), Alicia (Mariner Head of Data Products), Ravi (Platform), Tasha (Security), Ben (ML), Samir (SRE).

Summary: Walkthrough of Redwood runtime JSON/contract features, console demo for pilot setup, discussion of guardrails around function/tool calling, and compliance integrations (KMS, VPC). Agreed next steps: pilot SOW, perf benchmarks, security docs.

Topics: intro, pilot goals, JSON/response-contract demo (API + Console), safe invoke / tool routing, fallback strategies, deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance, pilot logistics.

00:00 Alicia: Hey thanks everyone for joining. We sent over a short agenda, we're particularly focused on making sure the model outputs can be treated as structured financial advisories without leaking PII, and we want predictable latency.
00:18 Maya (AE): Great, thanks Alicia. Quick intros then Jonah will take over for the demo. High level we're proposing a 4-week pilot — we'll show the console and API flows, JSON mode, typed responses and safe-invoke semantics.
00:36 Jonah (SE): Cool, jumping in. One thing up-front — when we say JSON mode we mean the runtime enforces the shape, and we support typed fallbacks so if a call fails we can return a structured error instead of raw text.
00:55 Ben (ML): How strict is that enforcement? Will the model sometimes still hallucinate keys?
01:11 Jonah: It can, especially on creative models, but the runtime uses a verifier+repair loop. If the verifier fails at parse time we attempt a constrained re-gen with the same prompt and then apply a schema-based repair. If that still fails we return a typed error object.
01:32 Ravi: That repair flow — does it increase tail latency a lot? Our 95th pct target is 300ms for short prompts.
01:44 Jonah: Good question. For short prompts typical re-gen adds on average 120-180ms. We can mitigate with prefix caching and a low-cost conservative model fallback. For the pilot we recommend measuring both success-rate of first-pass schema conformance and 95/99 latencies.
02:05 Tasha (Security): Also, how do you handle private tool calls? We have internal lookup tools that must not be exfiltrated.
02:18 Jonah: We support tool routing with policy tags — calls to internal APIs can be pinned to Private Redwood Dedicated or our Private deployment so KV cash and internal tools never traverse the public plane. Also we expose an allow-list + audit log for each tool invocation.
02:39 Alicia: Did you say KV cash?
02:42 Jonah: Sorry, KV cache. Transcription slip.
02:49 Leo (Console PM): I'll share Console now. Screen: Redwood Console > org: mariner-sandbox > Runtime tab. You can create a Response Contract: name, JSON schema, fallback policy (error object / safe-text), tool whitelist, and routing policy.
03:10 Leo: Notice the 'Execution Mode' toggle — Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private. For the pilot we usually do Hosted with VPC tunnel for the tool connections, or Dedicated if they need capacity guarantees.
03:32 Ravi: VPC tunnel meaning what exactly? Peering or IPsec?
03:36 Leo: We support VPC peering and IPsec-based tunnels depending on cloud. For on-prem we have an appliance option.
03:45 Samir: Any implications for egress logs and audit retention? We need retention for 2 years for some audits.
03:52 Tasha: That was my question as well.
03:55 Jonah: Audit logs are configurable. We stream to S3 or your SIEM; retention is a per-org setting. We also provide request-level redaction rules so PII can be masked before persistence.
04:15 Ben: Back to schema enforcement — can we embed typed enums for allowed merchant categories?
04:23 Jonah: Yes, enums and value sets are supported in the contract schema. We also support custom validators so you can run a small lambda-style validator on the verifier step (runs in the control plane, sandboxed).
04:40 Alicia: Any risk that the validator could block normal traffic? We can't have it be single-threaded choke point.
04:47 Jonah: Validators are async-ish — the verifier runs inline but validator calls are bounded (100ms default) and if they time out the contract falls back to the specified fallback policy. We can tweak that for the pilot.
05:05 Maya: Let's demo a sample API flow. Jonah will prompt via API and we'll show the streaming of a typed response into a downstream tool.
05:17 Jonah: (switch to API) Hitting POST /v1/generate with model: aurora-7b-redwood (quantized), mode: json, contract_id: MF-invoice-01, tool_whitelist: [internal-lookup, enrichment-api].
05:35 Jonah: Streaming response shows: {"action":"enrich","payload":{"merchant_id":"M123","category":"mortgage_advice","confidence":0.93}} then the runtime emits a tool-invoke event: tool=internal-lookup args={"merchant_id":"M123"}.
05:58 Ravi: The tool invoke arg — is that logged in plaintext?
06:04 Jonah: It's logged to audit with PII redaction enabled. The exact redaction rules are configurable.
06:12 Tasha: Can we enforce that some tools never appear in hosted logs? They must route through our VPC-only service.
06:19 Jonah: Yes — routing policy can pin particular tools to Private or Dedicated. If the runtime sees a mismatch it'll fail the request with an explicit routing error instead of invoking.
06:34 Ben: How are fallbacks composed if the tool fails? E.g., enrich fails — do you retry or return a partial structured result?
06:42 Jonah: You configure retries per-tool and a fallback contract. Typical pattern: 1 retry with exponential backoff, then return structured partial response with a 'tool_status' field and an 'error_code'.
06:58 Alicia: From a safety standpoint we need to avoid the model fabricating bank routing numbers. Do you scan for that?
07:06 Jonah: Yes — we have built-in PII detectors and you can add custom classifiers. Detected high-risk items trigger scrub/obfuscate or cause the output to be suppressed and routed to a human-review workflow.
07:24 Tasha: And encryption for keys? KMS? We need HSM-backed keys for production.
07:31 Jonah: We integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM for secrets at rest and support key rotation. We also sign tool invocation request tokens with a per-org key.
07:45 Maya: Quick pause — any concerns so far?
07:50 Alicia: The flow looks promising. Our big worries are latency, and making sure the fallback behavior doesn't surface as a poor customer experience.
08:02 Maya: For latency we suggest a two-pronged pilot: run a 24-hour synthetic steady-state load to measure baseline tokens/sec and tail latency, plus 3 targeted real-traffic windows with traffic replay. We'll instrument prefix caching hit rate and first-pass schema success.
08:22 Ravi: For compute — can you show quantization and batching settings?
08:27 Jonah: Sure. In Console > Model Profiles we have quantization presets (4-bit int8, dynamic FP16) and batching policies: continuous batching window and max batch size. We also surface cost estimates per 1M tokens for each profile.
08:45 Ben: If we choose a conservative model for first-pass and a cheaper fallback for repair, can the runtime orchestrate that automatically?
08:54 Jonah: Yes — we call that the 'verify-and-fallback chain' — policy defines primary model, retry model, and fallback artifact (typed error or cached response). Routing is local to a single request so you won't pay for multiple long-running invocations except when needed.
09:15 Samir: About metrics and traces — can we export per-token tracing to our internal tracing system?
09:22 Leo: We have tracing hooks and per-route perf breakdown; you can stream traces to Jaeger/Datadog. Token-level traces are sampled to control cost.
09:35 Alicia: On governance, can we have role-based controls so only product teams can update contracts?
09:40 Maya: Yes, RBAC with role sets: Admin, Contract Author, Viewer. We also support SSO (SAML/SCIM) and can map groups to roles.
09:55 Tasha: Does Redwood preserve raw prompts in logs? That's a no in our policy.
10:00 Jonah: By default prompts are logged but we can enable prompt redaction or prompt-hash-only mode. You'll have to assess the tradeoff vs observability.
10:15 Ben: Let's step through an end-to-end failure scenario: model returns malformed JSON, tool invocation times out, and then fallback returns an error to the customer.
10:27 Jonah: (demo) Step 1: malformed first-pass — verifier detects parse error, triggers re-gen. Step 2: re-gen fails -> validator times out -> fallback returns {"status":"partial","reason":"TOOL_TIMEOUT","details":{...}} and a non-200 API code. Console records event with links to the failed payload and suggested prompts to improve.
11:00 Alicia: Will that non-200 code break our frontend error handling?
11:05 Jonah: We can map fallback codes to HTTP 200 with an internal 'status' field if you prefer — that's configurable per-route.
11:14 Ravi: Pilot logistics — what's included in pilot pricing?
11:19 Maya: Pilot pricing includes reserved compute for the test window, 2 pilot-related support hours per week, and up to X tokens for benchmark. If you go Dedicated we shift to monthly commit. We'll include options in the SOW.
11:38 Alicia: Regarding competitors, we've evaluated Anthropic and in-house self-hosted. How do you compare?
11:46 Maya: Short answer: we focus on production patterns — stronger runtime controls, unified observability and routing, and the private deployment story. We'll share a short comparison doc.
11:58 Tasha: A few compliance items: we need the network diagram, SOC2 cert, list of subcontractors, and data flow showing what leaves our VPC.
12:08 Jonah: We'll attach those to the SOW.
12:15 Ben: Will you give us a sandbox org so we can try Console?
12:20 Leo: Yes I'll provision mariner-sandbox and invite Alicia+Ben+Ravi. You'll get full console read/write for the pilot scope.
12:30 Maya: Ok wrapping up — anything else?
12:33 Alicia: One ask — show us how the runtime handles mixed structured text responses, sometimes we want a short human sentence plus a JSON payload.
12:42 Jonah: We support hybrid payloads: a top-level 'text' and 'contract' fields, or attachments. The verifier runs against the contract portion.
12:52 Ravi: Good. Let's lock the SOW and kick-off next week.
12:58 Maya: Great. We'll send SOW, security pack, and schedule the kick-off. Thanks everyone.
13:05 Meeting end.
